newsitem.title: USA: New diagnostic tool for breast cancer reported.
newsitem.headline: New diagnostic tool for breast cancer reported.

text.p: A new technique to diagnose the spread of breast cancer could lead to more conservative surgical treatment of women with the disease, doctors said on Tuesday.
The technique combines a dye and mapping with a radioactive substance to find the "sentinel" or first lymph node in the armpit damaged by the cancer.

Treatment decisions are made on the basis of the state of the armpit lymph nodes, which can predict a victim's likely survival, said the report from the University of South Florida in Tampa published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.
"This strategy has the potential to decrease overall morbidity without compromising patient care," the study said.

"As with the institution of lumpectomy as a viable alternative to mastectomy (removal of all or part of the breast) for treating primary breast cancer, if these results are confirmed with other investigators lymphatic mapping and selective lymphadenectomy (removal) could lead to more conservative surgical treatment of women with breast cancer."
